headline: Redemption fears fade and money returns to rates; 10Y CCDC hits a 1-year low of 1.621%
summary: CGBs extended Monday's recovery as redemption pressure eased, with the long end retracing all of Friday's selloff in two sessions. The CCDC 10-year fell 1.3bp to 1.621%, a 1-year low, and the 30-year 1.5bp to 2.051%, while the 5-year led the belly, down 1.7bp to 1.331%, and the 1-year was flat at 1.170%. Policy banks kept pace: CDB 10-year fell 1.3bp to 1.658%, still 3.7bp over CGB, with ADBC and EXIM about 6.8bp and 5.9bp over; CDB 2-year fell 1.5bp, narrowing its spread to 13.4bp.
drivers: Zhuhai Huafa paid interest on two public bonds and wealth-product redemptions did not spread, so money that left bond funds on Friday came back to liquid rates bonds. Desks describe the redemptions as mainly pre-emptive and focused on credit and mixed bond funds. TL futures rose 0.48% and T futures 0.14%.
Stocks slip as support measures disappoint

The Shanghai Composite fell 0.7% to 3,614, giving back much of Monday's gain, even after regulators cut the buyback relending rate to 1% from 1.25%, made it permanent and ran a third swap-facility operation with over RMB100bn of applications. The equity-bond seesaw favoured bonds.

The PBOC ran RMB621bn of overnight reverse repos at 1.25% against RMB953bn maturing, a RMB332bn net drain. Overnight Shibor edged up 0.3bp to 1.289% and 7-day fell 2.1bp to 1.342%. The 1-year was flat, so the front end stays pinned to funding and gains came from 2Y out.
FX RRR hike to cool the yuan

The PBOC will raise the FX deposit reserve ratio to 6% from 4% from Nov 15, absorbing about $24bn, and the onshore yuan fell as much as 0.37% to 6.6728. It targets dollar liquidity, not yuan funding, so bonds shrugged it off; leaning against yuan strength leaves room for easy domestic policy. Supply was light: MoF 28- and 91-day bills cleared at 0.80% and 1.11%.
data: Oct RatingDog mfg PMI (Nov 2)
52.0 (f 51.6, p 52.1); output fastest since April; 11th month of expansion
Private and export-facing firms are holding up, which tempers the weak official print but did not stop the bond rally.
Oct official PMIs (Oct 31)
Mfg 49.3 (f 50.0, p 50.1); new orders 49.4; non-mfg 49.7 (p 50.2); composite 49.7
Back in contraction with softer prices, which supports low yields and the case for continued easy funding.
Q3 PBOC loan report (Oct 28)
Property loans RMB50.08tn, −5.2% y/y; mortgages RMB35.91tn, −4.1% y/y (−1.1tn YTD)
Households keep paying down mortgages, so credit demand stays weak and banks keep buying bonds.
Sep industrial profits (Oct 27)
A beat driven by AI hardware, metals and oil-linked prices, not households; bonds looked through it.
Oct MLF (Oct 26)
RMB700bn 1Y vs RMB900bn maturing (net −200bn); outright reverse repos +400bn net in Oct
A tidy-up, not tightening: medium-term liquidity is still up RMB200bn in October, and the overnight rate is now the policy signal.
Q3 GDP (Oct 19)
Firmer growth, near the bottom of the 4.5–5% target. It eases pressure for stimulus but was not strong enough to sell bonds.
Sep activity (Oct 19)
Growth is led by exports and AI-linked output, with households and property still weak. It does not challenge low yields.
view: Neutral leaning long for the next 1–2 weeks, with the 10-year expected in a 1.60–1.65% CCDC range. Funding is anchored at 1.25%, the credit scare has calmed, equities are struggling despite support and October data are likely soft, so the path of least resistance is still lower yields. But the 10-year is now at a 1-year low, 1.60% is a hard level, the 10Y long is close to its 1.61% target and November local bond supply is front-loaded, so I would take profit into 1.61% rather than chase. Stay overweight the 10-year against the rich 5–7Y belly, underweight policy banks against CGBs, neutral the 30-year. Fresh redemptions or a sharp equity rebound would take the 10-year back to 1.65%, while weak October trade, inflation or credit data could push it through 1.60%.

buckets.name: CGB 1–2Y
buckets.why: The 2-year fell 0.9bp to 1.227%, in the 2nd percentile of its 1-year range (average 1.310%), while the 1-year was flat at 1.170% with overnight Shibor at 1.289%. With the overnight policy rate at 1.25% and the PBOC draining surplus cash daily, the front end has little room left to rally.
buckets.call: Hold; add 2-year CGBs only above 1.27%, or if the overnight rate is cut below 1.25%.

buckets.name: CGB 5–7Y belly
buckets.why: The 5-year fell 1.7bp to 1.331% and the 7-year 1.2bp to 1.431%, both at 1-year lows. 2s5s10s is −18.7bp (0th percentile, average −7.6bp) and 5s7s10s −8.9bp (2nd percentile). The 5s10s flattener from ~29bp is flat at 29.0bp (76th percentile, average 26.4bp), inside the 31bp stop.
buckets.call: Keep the 5Y-into-10Y switch (5s10s flattener) from ~29bp, target 25bp, stop 31bp.

buckets.name: CGB 10Y
buckets.why: The long from 1.65% is 2.9bp in the money with the 10-year at 1.621%, 1.1bp from the 1.61% target; the 1.665% add level was never reached. It still screens cheap against neighbours: 7s10s20s is −23.3bp, in the 90th percentile against a −29.3bp average, though the outright level is at a 1-year low.
buckets.call: Long from 1.65%, target 1.61%; raise the stop to 1.65% to lock in the gain.

buckets.name: CGB 30Y
buckets.why: The 30-year fell 1.5bp to 2.051%, near its 1-year low of 2.041%, and 10s30s is 43.0bp, in the 27th percentile against a 45.6bp average. The 20-year at 2.043% is almost flat to the 30-year and 30s50s is 12.3bp (8th percentile), so the ultra-long block offers little cushion ahead of Nov–Dec supply.
buckets.call: Neutral. Add above 2.10% (10s30s ~46bp); poor risk/reward below 2.05%.

buckets.name: Policy banks 2–10Y vs CGB
buckets.why: CDB 10-year is 3.7bp over CGB, in the 4th percentile against a 9.9bp average, and the CDB 5-year spread is 10.2bp (6th percentile). The CDB 2-year spread narrowed 0.6bp to 13.4bp (4th percentile). The switch from ~3bp is open and 0.7bp in the money; EXIM's 1-year reopening at 1.3078% drew 3.8x cover, so demand is still firm.
buckets.call: Keep the CDB 10Y into CGB 10Y switch from ~3bp, target 8bp, stop 1bp.

buckets.name: ADBC/EXIM vs CDB 10Y
buckets.why: ADBC 10-year yields 3.1bp more than CDB, in the 75th percentile against a 1.3bp average; EXIM is 2.2bp over, near its 2.0bp average. The pickup reflects supply and liquidity after recent ADBC 10-year issuance, not credit.
buckets.call: Hold ADBC/EXIM 10Y rather than CDB 10Y for the ~2–3bp pickup.

buckets.name: Policy banks 20–30Y
buckets.why: CDB 20-year is 4.9bp over CGB, still at a 1-year low (0th percentile, average 10.7bp), and the 30-year 11.0bp, also at its 1-year low (average 12.7bp). Policy bank long bonds again moved one for one with CGBs, so the spread offers no cushion if supply picks up.
buckets.call: Prefer CGB 20–30Y to CDB 20–30Y; revisit policy bank long bonds above a 13bp 30-year spread.

cgb:1.note: Flat at 1.170% (+0.2bp), pinned near the 1.25% overnight policy rate.

cgb:2.note: Down 0.9bp to 1.227%, a 1-year low, as funding held near 1.25–1.29%.

cgb:5.note: Down 1.7bp to 1.331%, a 1-year low; led the belly and still the richest point on the curve.

cgb:10.note: Down 1.3bp to 1.621%, a 1-year low, fully retracing Friday's redemption-driven selloff.

cgb:30.note: Down 1.5bp to 2.051%; TL futures rose 0.48% as the long end led again.

cdb:2.note: Down 1.5bp to 1.362%; about 13.4bp over CGB, narrower by 0.6bp.

cdb:5.note: Down 1.0bp to 1.433%; about 10.2bp over CGB, near its 1-year tight.

cdb:30.note: Down 1.5bp to 2.161%; about 11bp over CGB, a 1-year tight.

adbc:10.note: Down 1.2bp to 1.689%; about 6.8bp over CGB, 3.1bp over CDB.

exim:10.note: Down 1.2bp to 1.680%; about 5.9bp over CGB, 2.2bp over CDB.

watch: Next: the US midterm results (Nov 4 Asia time), the RatingDog services PMI (Nov 4), US payrolls (Nov 6), October trade and FX reserves (Nov 7), October CPI/PPI and credit data the following week, front-loaded November local bond supply (about RMB611bn planned), and the FX RRR hike taking effect on Nov 15.
